about.title: Arcadia Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Arcadia draws steady foot traffic to spots along Huntington Drive and Baldwin Avenue, from the Westfield Santa Anita mall to smaller retail plazas and restaurants near Santa Anita Avenue. Wet floors, uneven walkways, poor lighting, and neglected maintenance in these busy spaces can turn an ordinary errand into a serious injury. Under California law, a property owner or manager can be held responsible if they knew, or reasonably should have known, about a hazardous condition and didn't fix it or warn visitors. Proving that notice is often the hardest part of a premises liability case, which is why quick action to document the scene and secure any surveillance footage matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free connection service that puts you in touch with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather evidence before it disappears, and explain your options at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Connect With an Attorney Through LawProactive

items.title: Notice Is Everything in These Cases
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew, or should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify inspection records, prior complaints, or maintenance logs that speak to that notice.

items.title: Video Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Arcadia retailers and property managers overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for not noticing a hazard, you can still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present your side clearly.

items.question: I slipped at a store near Westfield Santa Anita. What should I do first?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the exact spot, note the time, and ask an employee to file an incident report. Try to get names of any witnesses nearby, since foot traffic in that area is heavy and memories fade quickly. Then consider getting a free case review before evidence like surveillance video is lost.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall, though claims against a government-owned property, such as a city building or public sidewalk, have a much shorter notice deadline. Missing these windows can end your ability to recover, so it's worth checking your specific situation early.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after your case is reviewed.
